findings.text: observed['source'] and observed['target'] are captured inside while_held and never asserted, so the before-bytes snapshot the case reads guards nothing; a restore that fixed one sprint would be caught only by the final item assertions and recovered == [], not by the capture the comment implies is checked.

call_sites.detail: every plan-state write reaches the changed lock through project_state._resource_locks, used by write_resource, create_project_state, recover_project_state_transactions, move_sprint_item, push and close.

diff.detail: one commit, d900333f10, adds reckon/node_exclusive_lock.py and the probe, replaces the inline flock in project_state._resource_lock, adds the two-case test file and an evidence fragment; the journal-before-restore guard in recovery is untouched.

done_when.detail: the done_when asks for a two-node probe with differing hostnames and its base negative control plus thread and recovery tests; logs/head-probe.log and logs/base-probe.log name clu-3141 and clu-3142, logs/negative-control.log shows the two guarded ids red at base, and the head arm records 53 passed.

goal.detail: the goal is a plan-state lock that excludes a holder on another node, and reckon/node_exclusive_lock.py:60 adds fcntl.lockf to the flock that project_state._resource_lock takes, which is where reckon/project_state.py:2134 restores a journal and :2200 moves an item.

manifest.detail: the manifest records the head arm command and its 53-passed result, the base arm at 51, the importer arms at 10 failed / 555 passed and 8 failed / 559 passed, and names every log path the record cites.

write_paths.detail: the declared paths are project_state.py, one new module under reckon/, the probe under scripts/, the named test file and the evidence fragment; the diff of the commit touches exactly those five and nothing else.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_plan_state_lock_holds_on_every_node.py:131 and :179 assert a separate process is refused the POSIX record lock, and logs/negative-control.log records both reddening at the base revision with exactly those assertions.
justifications.evidence: logs/negative-control.log shows both guarded ids failing against the base tree and logs/head-probe.log and logs/base-probe.log show differing hostnames with refused versus acquired; the importer arms run in logs/importers-base.log and logs/importers-head.log with head failures a strict subset of base's.
justifications.fit: reckon/node_exclusive_lock.py follows the contextmanager shape and module-docstring idiom of the lock it replaces at reckon/_store.py:395, and no added name carries a plan label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/project_state.py:308 now takes reckon/node_exclusive_lock.exclusive_lock, which holds a POSIX record lock beside the flock, so the sprint locks that reckon/project_state.py:2134 and :2200 take before a restore or a move exclude a holder on another node.
justifications.reuse: no module owned a cross-node exclusive lock before this change; reckon/_store.py:395 _serialized_path_lock is the nearer owner and stays node-local, which plan section 4 accounts for rather than this node.
justifications.scope_discipline: all five paths in git diff 945e52f9..d900333f (reckon/project_state.py, reckon/node_exclusive_lock.py, scripts/plan_state_lock_probe.py, tests/test_a_plan_state_lock_holds_on_every_node.py, docs/evidence/fragments/a-plan-state-lock-holds-on-every-node/plan-state-lock-excludes-across-nodes.html) are inside the node's declared write paths.
